items.prompt: How confident are you that you could cut a big idea down to a first step you can finish this week?
You have a big app idea. Which first step is small enough to finish this week?

options.label: Sketch one screen of the idea on paper
Wait until you have better tools

items.explanation: A paper sketch takes one sitting and gives you something to react to, while the other options never finish or never start.

items.prompt: Write your current project idea in one line, then rewrite it as a first step small enough to do this week.

criteria: Reduces the idea to a single concrete task
Keeps the step doable within one week

items.prompt: In your own words, explain why a smaller first step helps you start a big idea.

criteria: Explains that a small step is finishable and produces something to react to
Contrasts it with a plan that never starts

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could notice your progress on a project and adjust your next step?
You finished one part of your project this week. What is the most useful next move?

options.label: Look at what changed, then pick the next small step
Start over with a bigger plan
Ignore it and keep going without checking

items.explanation: Reviewing what changed turns progress into a clear next step, while ignoring it or restarting wastes the work you did.

items.prompt: List what you finished this week on one side and what is still open on the other, then write one next step.

criteria: Lists at least one thing finished and one thing open
Ends with a single concrete next step

items.prompt: In your own words, explain how noticing progress helps you decide what to do next.

criteria: Describes reviewing what changed since last time
Connects that review to choosing the next step
